questions.question: 1. In image arithmetic, how are the corresponding pixels of two images combined during an arithmetic operation?

answers.b: By combining only the boundary pixels

explanations.a: Correct. Image arithmetic operations are performed independently on corresponding pixels of the input images.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Image arithmetic is not limited to boundary pixels.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Image arithmetic operates on pixel values and does not involve averaging image dimensions.
explanations.d: Incorrect. An arithmetic operation on pixel values does not by itself change the image resolution.

questions.question: 2. What is the valid pixel-value range of an 8-bit grayscale image?

explanations.b: Correct. An 8-bit image can represent pixel values from 0 through 2^8 - 1, which is 255.
explanations.a: Incorrect. The value 0 is also a valid pixel value in an 8-bit image.
explanations.c: Incorrect. The maximum value of an 8-bit image is 255, not 256.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Negative values are not part of the standard 8-bit image range.

questions.question: 3. Which image arithmetic operation always produces a non-negative result when applied to two image pixel values?

explanations.c: Correct. The difference operation uses the absolute value, |p - q|, so its result cannot be negative.
explanations.a: Incorrect. Subtraction can produce a negative value when the second pixel value is larger than the first.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Addition produces a non-negative result for non-negative input pixels, but it is not the operation specifically defined using the absolute difference.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Division does not use an absolute difference and its result depends on the numerator and denominator.

questions.question: 4. Two 8-bit images are added pixel-wise. What is the maximum possible value of a resulting pixel before any range adjustment is performed?

explanations.c: Correct. The maximum pixel value in each 8-bit image is 255, so the maximum sum is 255 + 255 = 510.
explanations.a: Incorrect. This is the maximum value of an individual 8-bit input pixel, not the maximum sum of two such pixels.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Adding two 8-bit pixel values can produce values considerably greater than 256.
explanations.d: Incorrect. 65025 is the maximum product of two 255-valued pixels, not their maximum sum.

questions.question: 5. What problem occurs when an arithmetic operation produces a pixel value greater than 255 for an 8-bit output image?

explanations.b: Correct. An overflow occurs when an arithmetic operation produces a value greater than the maximum representable value of the output image.
explanations.a: Incorrect. Underflow refers to a value falling below the minimum allowed pixel value.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Image segmentation is a separate image-processing task and does not describe a value exceeding the valid range.
explanations.d: Incorrect. A pixel value exceeding the valid range is a range problem, not a change in image resolution.

questions.question: 6. Which method maps the minimum and maximum values of an arithmetic result to 0 and 255, respectively, for an 8-bit output image?

explanations.d: Correct. Auto-scaling remaps the range of the arithmetic result so that its minimum and maximum values correspond to 0 and 255.
explanations.a: Incorrect. Subtraction is an arithmetic operation between image pixel values, not a method for remapping the output range.
explanations.b: Incorrect. Clipping limits values to the valid range but does not remap the entire range between its minimum and maximum values.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Difference is an arithmetic operation based on the absolute difference between corresponding pixels.

questions.question: 7. Two 8-bit images are multiplied pixel-wise. What is the maximum possible value of a resulting pixel before range adjustment?

explanations.c: Correct. The maximum input pixel value is 255, so the maximum product is 255 × 255 = 65025.
explanations.a: Incorrect. This is the maximum value of an individual 8-bit input pixel, not the maximum product.
explanations.b: Incorrect. 510 is the maximum sum obtained by adding two maximum-valued 8-bit pixels.
explanations.d: Incorrect. This value is not the maximum product of two 8-bit pixel values.

questions.question: 8. Consider two 8-bit images A and B. If A(x,y) = 40 and B(x,y) = 100, what is the output pixel value at (x,y) when the difference operation is applied?

explanations.a: Correct. The difference operation is |A(x,y) - B(x,y)| = |40 - 100| = 60.
explanations.b: Incorrect. The difference operation uses the absolute value, so its result is not negative.
explanations.c: Incorrect. 140 is the result of adding the two pixel values, not taking their absolute difference.
explanations.d: Incorrect. This value does not result from applying the difference operation to the given pixel values.

questions.question: 9. Why is a final range-adjustment step often required after performing arithmetic operations on 8-bit images?

answers.a: Because arithmetic operations always change the image dimensions
answers.b: Because the output may contain values outside the valid 8-bit range
answers.c: Because arithmetic operations cannot be performed pixel-wise
answers.d: Because all arithmetic operations produce only negative values

explanations.b: Correct. Arithmetic operations such as addition and multiplication can produce values outside the 0 to 255 range required for an 8-bit image.
explanations.a: Incorrect. Arithmetic operations on corresponding pixels do not inherently change the image dimensions.
explanations.c: Incorrect. Image arithmetic is specifically performed pixel-wise on corresponding pixels.
explanations.d: Incorrect. Arithmetic operations can produce positive, zero, or negative values depending on the operation and input values.
